P1.evidence: P1a hit: "So, Jared, I've been talking to Kim. You've spoken with him a few days ago, right?... So he briefed me in about your situation, but I'm kind of old school, you know, and I'd love to hear it from you." P1b partial — a three-part frame where the script asks for four: "What you're up to, what you've been doing, and how can we actually help you achieve your goals?" covers where you are and where you want to go, but never what is in the way or what you need. P1c partial — he got agreement ("Cool. Yeah. Sounds good.") but never asked for it; there was no "Does that work?" P1d hit — the open question is embedded in the same breath as the frame and it worked, producing a five-minute unprompted answer.

P2.evidence: Materially weaker than the discovery this rep is capable of. P2a miss — age was volunteered ("I'm 47, so I'm trying to, you know, get young, stay young") and never asked; height and current weight were never established at all, which for a body-composition goal is a real gap. P2b hit — the job was explored properly and the desk-bound question was asked: "probably a lot of sitting is going to be involved", answered "you're stuck to that desk for nine to 10 hours a day". P2c miss — health conditions, own or hereditary, were never asked. P2d hit, and asked twice: "Do you have any injuries? Or any limitations that are affecting your working?" then "Anything that limits your movements, any aches, any pains in your, I don't know, hips, lower back, the most common one." P2e partial — the training week emerged from the opening monologue but the rep never asked how many days he actually trains. P2f miss — results were volunteered ("I've been continuing to progress"). P2g partial — asserted from setter notes rather than asked: "Kim mentioned that you're already doing somewhat of a keto thing." P2h is an explicit and quotable miss: "Sleep, of course, I think I don't have to remind you of that." He named the check and skipped it. P2i miss — energy through the day never raised.

P3.evidence: The phase that carried the call. P3d hit, though telegraphed: "when I ask about the goals, the guys that I'm talking to, it's always like, what's the deeper why? So what is your deeper why?" It worked anyway and opened the divorce, the lost decade and the new chapter. He then followed properly — "when you think about it for a second, what becomes actually possible?" and "what would that moment actually be worth to you?" — and reached genuine depth: "it's redemption, right? I'm working towards redemption of all my pain, you know? It's not a small thing I'm trying to do." That is P3g hit on identity. P3a and P3c never asked. P3h partial — he labelled it back as "the Jared 2.0" and "we're getting from good to great" rather than running the "so this isn't really about the weight, it's about X, is that right?" confirmation. P3f is the notable miss: the prospect said his children had become distant from him and that a planned family travel life evaporated, and the rep never asked who else this impacts. He steered the impact question toward dating and travel instead, and the children were never returned to.

P4.evidence: Essentially unrun, and the most consequential gap on the call. P4a partial and P4d partial only because the prospect volunteered his own history unprompted in the opening monologue — free weights, push-pull-legs, keto, the schedule constraint. The rep asked none of it. He never asked what happened with those attempts, never asked why they did not stick, never let the prospect name the gap, and never ran P4f. This matters more here than on a typical call: the prospect self-programmes from Mike Matthews' books, has run 23:1 fasting windows and multi-day fasts, owns a well-stocked home gym and reports steady progress. The question of what he actually cannot do alone — the entire justification for the fee — was never asked once. He bought anyway, which is exactly the kind of outcome that should not be allowed to launder the process score.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame of any kind. The two-year question was never asked, there was no settle test, no "why not", and no line in the sand. The rep ran the mirror image instead — an upside frame ("when you visualize that, like, what would that moment actually be worth to you?") plus reassurance that things get better with age ("when I turned 40, for me, it was like a second wind"). The prospect supplied his own downside reasoning unprompted ("if you're not moving forward, you're moving backwards, right? Especially in health and fitness"), which the rep accepted rather than developed. Because no cost of inaction was ever established, there was nothing to fall back on when the budget hesitation arrived at 00:40, and the rep had to solve it purely with payment mechanics.

P6.evidence: P6a hit and well placed, immediately before the price: "just to make sure we're on the same page, if you had the right training, the simple nutrition and accountability from Trevor, do you feel that you would get to that version 2.0 of Jared, that confident on a journey for a better future?" Answer: "Yeah, absolutely. Absolutely." P6b never asked — and this is the specific omission that cost him a clean close, because "if you had everything you needed, is there any reason you wouldn't go all in" would have surfaced the pay cut before the price rather than after it. P6c partial: he had a yes, but a qualified one — "I feel, you know, I'm most of the way there, but I just got to put the pieces together" — and he moved to price on it. Hesitation then surfaced within seconds and he did not return to Phase 5, though in fairness there was no Phase 5 to return to.

P11.evidence: The most complete P11 execution in this batch. P11a hit — payment taken live, "Let me go get my wallet in a minute" then "i see it went through okay". P11b hit — Trevor's calendar checked on the call, Monday 29th at 3:15pm Eastern agreed, and the confirmation email verified in real time ("please check your email for the confirmation on the onboarding session with Trevor" / "Yep, I got it"). He also caught and reconciled a mismatch between the payment email and the email on file, and re-verified the phone number. P11c hit — agreement confirmed as received and signed on the call: "Yeah, I think I got it. Sign now" / "You sign document" / "Yep." P11d partial — he covered the onboarding questionnaire ("there's going to be also an onboarding form. So please take a few minutes to fill it out before talking with Trevor") and referenced the community as an "invitation to Primal University", but never told him to read the welcome email and never walked him to a community link or confirmed he had joined.

objection_plays.detail: Trigger at 00:40:31 on budget. The rep opened correctly with the isolation move — "let me just be sure. You're 100% sure on this?" — and got "I'm 100% sure", which unlocked the pay-cut disclosure. He then ran the break-it-up move almost to script: "most of the guys just put it on a credit card upfront, but we're flexible." From there the play thins out. He never asked permission for the open, honest financial conversation. Of the six financial-picture items he ran a partial version of exactly one — credit cards, and only usage and comfort ("do you use credit cards at all?", "how do you feel about using that?"), not how many, not available credit per card, not used versus available. Cash on hand, monthly surplus after bills, and crypto or investments were never asked. The income figures came out because the prospect volunteered them. He also never used the "you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place" reframe. It closed on payment mechanics rather than on the play, and it closed because the prospect had savings and low resistance, not because the play was run.

The words were present — "let me think about and look at the budget a little bit" — but the rep read the substance correctly as money, not deliberation, and routed to OC instead. None of the OA moves ran. Scored a miss for completeness rather than as a criticism: the diagnosis was right and running OA here would have been the wrong play.
Prospect is divorced and single; no partner consult exists as a decision path.

No timing objection was raised. The imminent four months of classroom training is the reverse — the prospect presented it as the reason he needs short daily workouts now: "that's exactly what I need right now because I'm gonna be, you know, in class five days a week."

No fear or doubt about the modality. He arrived pre-sold from Trevor's Instagram and reinforced it himself: "just the more efficient and less equipment approach of kettlebell, if I could master that, then, you know, that'd be fantastic."

notes: A close that the process did not earn. P4 and P5 were not run at all and P2 was thin, yet it closed in 51 minutes at full price because the prospect was pre-sold by Instagram, pre-qualified by the setter, sits squarely in the ICP and has savings. The coaching point is the one question never asked: this man programmes himself out of Mike Matthews books and has done multi-day fasts, so what exactly can he not do alone? Never establishing that left the fee resting on nothing but goodwill, and it is the reason the price landed on a hesitation rather than on a yes. Separately, tighten P1b to four parts and stop skipping sleep out loud — "Sleep, of course, I think I don't have to remind you of that" is a check being waved away on the recording.
